intro: DEMO CONTENT — this guide exists to show every editorial field the guide page can render. The tools are placeholders and the advice is illustrative.

A walkthrough video lets buyers see how the rooms connect before they book a viewing. This demo shows how a guide walks a reader from a folder of listing photos to one finished video, with a tool attached to each step and a reason for each tool.
learningOutcomes: How to prepare listing photos so the video steps have good input
How to turn single photos into short clips with a prompt
How to assemble clips into one walkthrough with music and captions
How to check the result before you publish it

beforeYouStart.title: Your listing photos
beforeYouStart.description: Interior and exterior shots, in the order a visitor would walk through the home.

beforeYouStart.title: Permission to use the photos
beforeYouStart.description: Check you have the rights to edit and publish them.

beforeYouStart.title: About 30 minutes
beforeYouStart.description: Most of it is waiting for clips to generate.

steps.title: Prepare the photos
steps.body: Pick the shots, put them in walking order, and fix exposure so every room looks consistent.
instructions: Choose one or two photos per room.
Rename them 01, 02, 03… in the order a visitor walks through.
Straighten verticals and even out the brightness across the set.

tools.name: Example Photo Editor
tools.why: Batch edits keep lighting consistent, so the clips cut together without jumps in brightness.

steps.expectedOutcome: A numbered folder of evenly lit photos, one route through the home.
tips: Leave out near-duplicate angles — they make the video feel slow.

alternatives.name: Example Mobile Photo App
alternatives.why: Fine for a handful of photos on the go.

steps.title: Generate a clip from each photo
steps.body: Upload each photo and use the prompt to turn it into a short, steady camera move.
instructions: Open the video generator and start a new image-to-video project.
Paste the prompt below and generate.
Repeat for each photo, keeping the same prompt so the motion matches.

tools.name: Example Video Generator
tools.why: It turns a still photo into a few seconds of camera movement — the core of the walkthrough.

steps.prompt: Create a slow, steady walkthrough clip from this photo. Gentle forward camera movement, natural lighting, no people, no text, no added furniture.
steps.expectedOutcome: One short clip per photo, all with the same slow camera movement.
tips: Keep the prompt identical across photos so the clips feel like one shoot.
Regenerate any clip that invents objects that are not in the room.

steps.title: Assemble the walkthrough
steps.body: Put the clips in walking order and join them with simple transitions.
instructions: Import every clip into the video editor.
Order them by the numbers from step 1.

tools.name: Example Video Editor
tools.why: Sequencing and transitions happen on a timeline, which the generator does not have.

steps.expectedOutcome: One continuous video that moves room to room in order.
tips: Keep the total under a minute for social posts.

steps.title: Add music, captions and check it
steps.body: Add a quiet music bed and room captions, then watch it through once before publishing.
instructions: Add a music track and lower it so it sits under everything else.
Watch the whole video once and compare every room against the real photos.

tools.name: Example Video Editor
tools.why: Music and captions go on the same timeline as the clips.

steps.expectedOutcome: A finished walkthrough video, checked against the real rooms.

tips: Shoot or choose photos with the same time of day, so the light matches from room to room.
Say clearly in the listing that the video was generated from photos.

commonIssues.problem: A clip adds furniture or objects that are not in the room
commonIssues.solution: Regenerate it, and keep "no added furniture" in the prompt. Never publish a clip that misrepresents the property.

commonIssues.problem: The camera movement differs from clip to clip
commonIssues.solution: Use the exact same prompt for every photo, and prefer photos taken from a similar height.
Go back to step 1 and even out the exposure across the photo set before generating.
